clue.text: Youthful person given minute by the clock

parts.note: minute in the sense of tiny, as a baby thing is very small
a clock's dial is its face

explanation.surface: A young person is handed a minute by the clock, as if timing a task.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minute' is the adjective (tiny), not sixty seconds, despite the clock beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with a babyface looks boyish or girlish, a youthful-looking person.

clue.text: European bodice

definitions.meaning: a native of the region straddling the western Pyrenees between Spain and France
a close-fitting women's jacket or bodice extending over the hips

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a people of the western Pyrenees and a tight-fitting bodice garment.

clue.text: Plead for some baseball, for a start

parts.note: to plead is to beg
an inning is one division of a baseball game, so part of it

explanation.surface: Someone pleads for a bit of baseball to get things started.
explanation.definitionFit: A start is the opening or commencement, a synonym.

clue.text: Equipped diver with fastening device on island

parts.note: a frog is an ornamental coat fastening of a loop and toggle
the Isle of Man, in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: A diver is kitted out with a clasp while on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: A frog is a braided loop-and-button coat fastening; the Isle of Man lies between Britain and Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A scuba diver equipped with wetsuit and flippers, especially a military one, is so called.

clue.text: Summoned to court and seen in hearing

indicators.note: in hearing means the word is taken as heard spoken rather than as written

parts.note: seen means sighted

explanation.surface: Someone is called to court and observed at the hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hearing' looks like the court session, but 'in hearing' signals a sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: To be named in a legal summons and required to appear is to be cited.

clue.text: Notes drink 'with stimulant removed

parts.note: D, E and C are three musical notes of the scale
A, F and F are three more musical notes

explanation.surface: Notes about a drink with its stimulant taken out.
explanation.walkthrough: Every letter here is a musical note name, D E C A F F, so 'Notes' supplies the whole word.
explanation.definitionFit: Decaff is coffee from which the caffeine, a stimulant, has been taken out.

clue.text: Say "I most abominably, showing this?

parts.note: say means for example, abbreviated eg

indicators.note: abominably means badly, so the letters of I most are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone who keeps saying 'I' in the worst way displays a certain vice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abominably' turns I MOST into ITSM after EG; the whole clue also describes the vanity of constantly saying 'I'.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-centredness shown by excessive talk about oneself is the vice described.

clue.text: Soon absorbing one sort of atom

indicators.note: absorbing means the first word takes the second inside it

parts.note: anon is an old word for soon
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Before long an atom takes something in.
explanation.definitionFit: A negatively charged ion is an atom (or group) that has gained electrons.

clue.text: Fail to contain City's initial fluent skill

indicators.note: to contain means the first word holds a letter taken from the next

parts.note: City as written

indicators.note: initial means the first letter of City

explanation.surface: Someone fails to hold on to City's opening fluent talent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to contain' works on the run of the two words: the initial letter shifts forward into the first word, so 'fluent' belongs to the definition, not an anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Facility is ease or aptitude in doing something, a smooth talent.

clue.text: Dicky 'seen warm in this, perhaps?

indicators.note: dicky means shaky or unsound, so the letters of seen warm are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man in a shirt-front is spotted warm in this sort of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: A dicky is also a detachable shirt-front, an example of the clothing that the anagram gives.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothing for men, such as a shirt-front, is the category.

clue.text: Lion house, for example

parts.note: not a zoo enclosure: Leo the Lion is one of the twelve astrological divisions, which astrologers also call houses

explanation.definitionFit: Leo, the Lion, is one of the twelve astrological divisions of the zodiac.

clue.text: Mundane collection, lacking style

indicators.note: collection suggests the letters of Mundane gathered up and put back together in a new order

explanation.surface: A dull assortment with no flair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'style' here is a verb's noun sense, a name or title: to style someone is to name them.
explanation.definitionFit: A style is a title or name, so lacking one means having no name.

clue.text: Plant featured in talk about garden borders

indicators.note: about means the first word goes round the next pieces

parts.note: spiel is glib talk

indicators.note: borders means the first and last letters of garden

explanation.surface: A plant comes up in conversation about the edges of a garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals the container; spignel (baldmoney) is an obscure herb, so the wordplay has to carry the solver.
explanation.definitionFit: Spignel, or baldmoney, is an aromatic umbelliferous herb of mountain pasture.

clue.text: Major report provided for VIP

parts.note: major means big
a report is a loud noise, like a gunshot

explanation.surface: An important announcement made for a dignitary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'report' is the bang of a gun, not a document.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean an important, influential person, slang equivalent.

clue.text: Pictures of mature insects

definitions.meaning: pictures as a verb, forms a mental image
the plural of imago, the adult winged stage of an insect

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb meaning envisages and the plural of imago, an adult insect.

clue.text: Satisfied about religious text for choral composition

indicators.note: about means the first word goes around the second

parts.note: to satisfy a need is to meet it, so met
OT is the Old Testament

explanation.surface: Content with a scriptural passage set for a choir.
explanation.definitionFit: A motet is a short sacred piece for unaccompanied voices.

clue.text: Garment fully covering female and supported by guys?

definitions.text: Garment fully covering female and supported by guys?

parts.words: Garment fully covering female and supported by guys?
parts.note: a loose, flared frock that hides the wearer's shape, pictured jokingly as a canvas shelter held up by guy ropes

explanation.definitionFit: A loose dress widening from the shoulders, shaped like a tent, which is held up by guy ropes.

clue.text: Is insulting about bill they calculate

indicators.note: about means the first word goes round the second

parts.note: is insulting means abuses
ac, short for account, is a bill

explanation.surface: Someone is rude about the bill those reckoners totted up.
explanation.definitionFit: An abacus is a counting frame of beads used for arithmetic, so these devices compute.

clue.text: What fisherman reportedly wants in the bay

indicators.note: reportedly means the word is said aloud, not as written

parts.note: an angler hopes for a fish to take the bait, a bite

explanation.surface: An angler hopes for a nibble in the bay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wants' links the angler to what they want; the sound-alike is that nibble on the line.
explanation.definitionFit: A bight is a curved stretch of coast forming a wide bay.

clue.text: Part of mosaic showing Greek god put up

indicators.note: up, in a down clue, means the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: Ares is the Greek god of war
to put is to set

explanation.surface: A mosaic shows a Greek god being raised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns ARES and SET together, giving TES SERA.
explanation.definitionFit: A tessera is one small square tile of the many in a mosaic.

clue.text: Bitterness as I am trapped by a companion

indicators.note: trapped by means the preceding words sit inside the following one

parts.note: a crony is a close companion
I am shortens to I'm

explanation.surface: A person resents being trapped by a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trapped by' signals the container; 'as' is only a link, not part of the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrimony is harsh, resentful ill-feeling, a synonym.

clue.text: Climbed on one's high horse, perhaps

definitions.meaning: climbed as in got up on to something
literally sitting on a tall horse, like a rider in the saddle

explanation.definitionFit: The word means climbed up on and also seated on horseback, as a rider is.

clue.text: Person' who doesn't approve of Sheridan's comedy

definitions.meaning: The ___, a 1779 satirical play by Richard Brinsley Sheridan

explanation.definitionFit: A faultfinder, and the title of Sheridan's 1779 farce about theatre.

clue.text: Huge figures in cost I added to business

parts.note: co is short for company, a business
a cost is a loss, as in at a cost

explanation.surface: Giant statues counted as a loss to a company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link here, and 'added to' puts the business abbreviation first, ahead of the cost and the I.
explanation.definitionFit: Colossi are gigantic statues, like the Colossus of Rhodes.

clue.text: Take part in poll anonymously, that's plain

indicators.note: Take part in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Vote without your name in a straightforward ballot.
explanation.walkthrough: LLANO is a South American treeless grassland.
explanation.definitionFit: A llano is a broad treeless grassy expanse of Latin America, a flat open grassland.

clue.text: Safer part? Nothing in it

indicators.note: in it means the zero sits inside the word for part

parts.note: to part is to sunder
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A safer part has nothing in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part' is a verb, separate, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Sounder means more secure or reliable, so less risky.

clue.text: State of confusion that upsets upper-class supporters

indicators.note: upsets, in a down clue, sets upper-class supporters upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: U means upper-class
fans are supporters

explanation.surface: A chaotic situation that upsets posh fans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsets' turns U FANS upside down in this down clue; U is the classic abbreviation for upper-class.
explanation.definitionFit: A snafu is a chaotic, botched situation, from military slang.

clue.text: US government organisation, say, to retire employees before time

parts.note: to say is to state
to retire is to depart
employees are men, workers

explanation.surface: A US body says that employees will retire early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' merely places MEN ahead of T.
explanation.definitionFit: The US federal department for foreign affairs, headed by the Secretary of State.

clue.text: Strike forcefully with an old-fashioned war cry

parts.note: to slog is to hit hard

explanation.surface: Hitting hard to an archaic battle shout.
explanation.walkthrough: A slogan was originally a Scottish Highland battle cry.
explanation.definitionFit: A clan's rallying shout in battle is the original Gaelic sense of slogan.

clue.text: Wrongly accused learner after crashing in obstructed road

indicators.note: crashing in means the learner forces its way into the middle
wrongly means the letters of accused are put in a different order

parts.note: L is a learner, from the L-plate

explanation.surface: A wrongly accused learner driver after a crash in a blocked road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrongly' makes CUDESAC from ACCUSED; 'crashing in' puts L inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A cul-de-sac is a dead-end street, closed at one end.
